issue.title: Agent dismiss does a synchronous notification-store write and full-store read on the UI thread
issue.description: Discovered by the sase-1d7 land agent (sase-1d7.land) on 2026-09-30 at master 788a9311f8 during epic verification; the sase-1d7.12 phase plan (core_unread_ack_index.md) explicitly deferred moving these callers.

task_type_fields.impact: Every agent dismiss on the default Agents tab does UI-thread notification-store I/O that scales with the store (about 5 MB / 1.5k rows after the sase-1d7 diet, previously 19 MB). That is a visible hitch per dismiss and violates the tui_perf placement rule that the sase-1d7 epic applied to acks.
task_type_fields.repro:
Dismissing agents from the Agents tab (`x` single dismiss in `_dismissing.py:~375`, bulk dismiss in `_dismissing.py:~223`, and save-and-dismiss in `_marking.py:~150`) calls `_dismiss_agent_completion_notifications_for_dismissed_agents` (`src/sase/ace/tui/actions/agents/_unread_state.py:382`) on the UI thread. That method:

1. calls `sase.notifications.dismiss_agent_completion_notifications_matching_agents(...)` synchronously, a Rust read-modify-write of the whole notification store under its lock; then
2. calls `self._refresh_notification_count()` (`_notification_polling.py:344`), which does a synchronous full-store read via `_read_notification_snapshot_from_provider()` on the UI thread.

Read the code path, or set `SASE_TUI_PERF`/`tui_trace` and dismiss an agent on a store of a few thousand rows: the dismiss key blocks the main loop for the Rust write plus a full snapshot parse.

Root cause: epic sase-1d7 moved only the read-side ack paths (`,u`, `,j`, row select) onto the coalescing ack writer (`_unread_ack_writer.py`, one `ack_agent_completions` Rust call per batch, cache removal by returned ids, async guarded resync). Its core-unread-ack-index phase plan explicitly left the dismiss callers on the old synchronous path ("Do not move those callers in this tale"). Fix: route explicit dismissal through the same worker (or `ack_agent_completions` off-thread), remove returned ids from the cached snapshot, and replace `_refresh_notification_count()` with the guarded `_refresh_notification_count_async`, following the sase-1d7 ack-pipeline design and tests (`tests/ace/tui/test_unread_ack_pipeline.py` has a main-thread-read guard to copy).

issue.creation_reason: Found while landing epic sase-1d7: its ack pipeline moved read-side acks off the UI thread but deliberately left the explicit-dismiss path on synchronous store I/O, so dismissing agents still hitches the TUI.

payload.description: Epic whose ack pipeline (_unread_ack_writer, ack_agent_completions) this dismiss path should reuse
